CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR MARCH 31, 2021 AT 8:00 A.M. WILL TAKE PLACE
SOLELY BY VIDEOCONFERENCE/TELECONFERENCE.
In order to facilitate public participation at meetings held solely by
electronic means, the City will accept public comment in the following manner:
1. During the meeting, members of the public may provide live public comment by
submitting a speaker card prior to the start of public comment on that item, at
the following webpage:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
If a public comment speaker wishes to speak on more than one agenda item, please
indicate so on the online form (multiple item speakers will be handled according
to the process posted on the agenda and as specified in the City Council meeting
policy). Public comments are limited to 3 minutes each, and the Mayor and City
Council may limit this time if reasonable under the circumstances.
2. If a public comment speaker needs assistance in completing a speaker card,
please call the Speaker Card Help phone number at: (626) 744-7660. Help line
will open 30 minutes prior to the start of the meeting.
After submitting a public speaker card, join the virtual meeting after the
published start time with a computer, other electronic device, or by telephone.
The same name or telephone number on the Speaker Card should be used for the
virtual meeting in order to locate and unmute the speaker.
Computer or electronic devices, join the meeting at:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Telephone only dial-in: 1-669-900-6833, Meeting ID: 161 482 446
3. Members of the public may submit correspondence of any length prior to the
start of the meeting, at the following email address:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
Correspondence will be forwarded to the City Council prior to the start of the
meeting, posted online, and made part of the legislative record for the item.

CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  March 31, 2021 - 8:00 A.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING WITH
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY SUPERVISOR KATHRYN BARGER

  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called to order the special joint meeting with Los
  Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger at 8:06 a.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Kennedy.

ROLL CALL:
 Councilmembers:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  DISCUSSION REGARDING FEDERAL COVID RELIEF
  FUNDING AND COORDINATION BETWEEN COUNTY AND
  CITY

  Supervisor Barger thanked the City Council and City Manager
  Mermell for their coordinated efforts working together with the
  Los Angeles County to address COVID-19 impacts. She stated
  that the City will receive a direct allocation of COVI D-19 relief
  funds within a two-year period; that she is willing to work with the
  City to determine what additional resources might be available
  to the City of Pasadena; and her goal in reaching out to the
  various Chambers of Commerce to reimburse and help jump
  start the economy, including small businesses, and non-profit
  organizations, that have been disproportionally impacted due the
  pandemic; and responded to questions.

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, provided information on staffs
  discussions with County staff, with the support of Supervisor
  Barger, to work together to ensure the residents of Pasadena

Council Minutes  03/31/2021
   receive the same level of support and opportunity to participate
  in federal relief programs and funding; and responded to
  questions.

  Mayor Gordo spoke in favor of the City coordinating with the Los
  Angeles County, particularly related to programming and young
  people (i.e. better programs and staffing at city parks).

  Councilmember Masuda requested that the Los Angeles County
  staff consider including fitness centers, spas, and yoga studios
  in their Personal Care and Retail Recovery grant program.

  Councilmember Williams echoed Councilmember Masuda's
  comments related for the need for funds to assist fitness centers,
  spas, and yoga studios; and suggested that funding be made
  available to assist those business with implementing preventive
  measures to keep the population safe and healthy.

  Councilmember Kennedy advocated for funding from Supervisor
  Barger for Robinson Park to provide a pool and pool house for
  young members of the community who are economically
  impacted by the pandemic.

  Supervisor Barger responded that her staff will reach out to City
  Manager Mermell to provide information on Los Angeles
  County's recreation grant programs that might be utilized for
  Robinson Park pool funds.

  Mayor Gordo asked staff to also apply for funds for the Villa
  Parke pool, which is also in need of repairs.

  Councilmember Williams and Vice Chair Wilson spoke on the
  need for Los Angeles County staff to strategically consider the
  shift to a remote workforce and the impacts to the economy (i.e.
  invest in high quality jobs, training to accommodate the adjusted
  work environment, how to support bioscience types of
  employment, development, housing availability, etc.).

  Councilmember Hampton advocated for funding for the City's
  Summer Rose Youth Program, which provides employment
  opportunities for Pasadena Unified School District (PUSD) high
  school students that reside in Altadena, Pasadena and Sierra
  Madre.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

Council Minutes  2  03/31/2021
   UPDATE ON VACCINATION EFFORTS IN PASADENA

  Dr. Ying Ying Goh, Director of Public Health and Health Officer,
  provided an update on the number of Pasadenans who have
  received the COVID-19 vaccination and the breakdown of the
  data by race, ethnicity, and age; mass vaccination strategies;
  coordination efforts with the County; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy thanked Dr. Goh for her leadership
  throughout the COVI D-19 pandemic crisis.

  Councilmember Hampton spoke on the need for additional
  Covid-19 vaccination outreach to the Latinx community; and
  reiterated his suggested door-to-door approach to distribute
  vaccinations.

  Supervisor Barger recommended that Pasadena's Vaccination
  strategy include evening and weekend appointments for those
  individuals who are unable to miss work to get vaccinated. She
  provided information on Los Angeles County's decision to align
  to the Orange Tier of the State's Blueprint for a Safer Economy;
  and responded to questions.

  Councilmember Williams spoke on the need to support and
  expand the City's local health activities and programs.

  Councilmember Rivas suggested a vaccination outreach
  program at the Department of Children and Family Services
  (DCFS) Pasadena site as a joint collaboration effort with the City
  and Los Angeles County.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, reported that one email expressing
  concerns related to the COVID-19 vaccination distribution was
  received by an anonymous individual, which was distributed to
  the City Council, posted on-line, and made part of the public
  record.

  Mayor Gordo summarized the follow-up items for the City and Los
  Angeles County staff as follows: vaccination efforts with DCFS
  office, City/County coordinated vaccination efforts, coordination
  of programs at local parks and community centers, possible
  funding for community pools; grant funding for Robinson Park
  and Villa Parke pool projects, and other parks in the City; job
  training efforts; and programming for PUSD after school and
  summer school. He also spoke on the need to address the
  importance of the Rose Bowl Stadium to the region and stated
  that he looks forward to a discussion on the matter at the next
  Rose Bowl Operating Company Board (RBOC) meeting
  scheduled for April 15, 2021.

Council Minutes  3  03/31/2021
   Supervisor Barger stated that she would like to include
  coordination efforts with the Boys and Girls Clubs located in
  Pasadena.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

  DISCUSSION REGARDING HERITAGE SQUARE SOUTH
  APPLICATION FOR LOS ANGELES COUNTY AFFORDABLE
  HOUSING FUNDS

  City Manager Mermell provided introductory comments, and
  William Huang, Director of Housing, presented a PowerPoint on
  the item; and responded to questions.

  Supervisor Barger provided information on County project,
  including current funding, which is the Lincoln Avenue Senior
  Apartment in Altadena. She spoke on the importance of providing
  housing for the senior population; and stated that she is open to
  working with the City of Pasadena and will ask her department to
  rethink the home fund allocation for the upcoming year, stating
  that she will provide an update within two weeks; and responded
  to questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the importance of providing
  affordable housing funds towards the Heritage Square South
  project for seniors, and asked Supervisor Barger for her
  assistance in securing the necessary funds to complete the
  project.

  The following individuals provided comments on the matter:

  Areta Crowell, Pasadena resident
  Jill Shook, Pasadena resident

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

  UPDATE AND INFORMATION ON MENTAL HEALTH
  SERVICES PROVIDED BY LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  DEPARTMENT OF MENTAL HEALTH

  Areta Crowell, Pasadena resident, advocated for additional
  outreach and supportive services for homeless population
  in the City of Pasadena.

  Supervisor Barger provided information on County staff seeking
  models that will replaces law enforcement and instead provides
  additional mental clinicians to conduct mental health outreach in

Council Minutes  4  03/31/2021
   the homeless population and throughout the community. She is
  working with school districts in terms of linking mental health
  services with the school districts recognizing that such services
  may be linked to families in the community.

  Mayor Gordo asked Supervisor Barger to ensure that County
  mental health staff and professionals attend a future City Council
  meeting to provide information on the various County portals and
  programs available to those in need of mental health services,
  including details and information for residents of Pasadena on
  how to access mental health services; and determine how best
  to provide mental health services to children and adults who are
  struggling with mental health issues as a result of COVID-19.

  Supervisor Barger committed to having staff present the
  requested information at a future City Council meeting as
  detailed above.

  Vice Mayor Wilson agreed with Mayor Gordo and spoke on the
  need for Los Angeles County staff to work directly with the
  school districts to provide mental health services to the youth
  who have been most impacted by COVID pandemic.

Councilmember Madison was  Councilmember Williams stated that she believes it would be
excused and disconnected  helpful if the City employed social workers and mental health
from the meeting at 9:38 a.m.  staff assigned to the City's Public Health Department as
  opposed to strictly relying on services from LA County. She also
  spoke on the need for police dispatch employees to be trained
  on understanding and identifying mental health issues when
  receiving calls for assistance.

  Councilmember Hampton asked staff (both City and LA County)
  to provide training to school and program staff to
  recognize/identify potential mental health issues that children
  attending after-school and summer school programs may be
  suffering from and experiencing.

  Supervisor Barger stated that she has reached out to PUSD
  program providers to work with them to ensure they are prepared
  to provide students the space and opportunity to express
  themselves, and will provide an update to the City Council on
  PUSD's preparedness to address such matters.

  Mayor Gordo stated that staff should also include options for the
  private schools in the City to ensure access to mental health
  services for all students. He stated that he will work with the City
  Manager and Supervisor Barger to provide an update on access
  to mental health services or portals; mental health services for
  PUSD and private schools; mental health services specifically
  impacted by COVID-19 and particularly as we move out of the
  COVI D pandemic; and "bed availability" for constituents with
  mental health emergencies.

Council Minutes  5  03/31/2021
   Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

  UPDATE ON DEVIL'S GATE DAM RESTORATION PROJECT

  Nina Chomsky, representing the Linda Vista-Annandale
  Association, expressed concerns with dust control and
  diesel truck exhaust impacts, and provided comments
  related to the project.

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, reported that a number of letters and
  emails  expressing  concerns  and  providing
  comments/suggestions on the matter were received, distributed
  to the City Council, posted on-line, and made part of the public
  record from the following individuals:

  Nina Chomsky, representing the Linda Vista-Annandale
  Association
  Elizabeth Krider, La Canada resident
  Esther Kornfeld, Pasadena resident
  Blair, representing Hahamongna Accountability Project
  Darren Dowell, Pasadena resident
  Marnie Gaede, La Canada resident

  Supervisor Barger provided information on her staff's actions to
  address, follow-up, and closely monitor the work of the Public
  Work's staff related to the Devil's Gate Dam Restoration project,
  and will review the issues stated in public comment and the
  correspondence regarding idling trucks and dust control; and
  responded to questions.

  Mayor Gordo requested that future updates on the Devil's Gate
  Dam Restoration project are presented to the Public Safety
  Committee.

  Councilmember Hampton thanked Supervisor Barger for her
  representation on the project to ensure the mitigations are being
  managed; and spoke on the need for City staff to hold the Los
  Angeles County Public Work's staff accountable in terms of
  adhering to the agreed upon mitigation measures.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

  UPDATE ON RECENT REVIEW AND ACTION RELATED TO
  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES INSPECTOR GENERAL'S
  SECOND INTERIM REPORT ON IMPROVING OVERSIGHT

Council Minutes  6  03/31/2021
   AND ACCOUNTABILITY WITHIN SKILLED  NURSING
  FACILITIES, DATED FEBRUARY 2021

  Due to time restraints, the item above was not discussed; and will
  be agenized at a future City Council meeting.

ADJOURNMENT  On order of the Mayor, the special joint meeting of the City
  Council adjourned at 10:09 a.m. in memory of all those that are
  ill and have lost their lives during the COVID-19 pandemic.

  Victor M. Gordo, May
  City of Pasadena
